# ggmosaic

ggmosaic was designed to create visualizations of categorical data and
is capable of producing bar charts, stacked bar charts, mosaic plots,
and double decker plots.

## Installation

You can install ggmosaic from github with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("haleyjeppson/ggmosaic")
```

## Example

``` r
library(ggmosaic)
library(dplyr)
gg <- happy %>% 
  mutate(finrela = forcats::fct_recode(finrela,
    "far below     " = "far below average",
    "    below" = "below average",
    "average" = "average",
    "above    " = "above average", 
    "l\n   far above" = "far above average")) %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_mosaic(aes(x = product(finrela), fill=health), show.legend = FALSE) +
  theme_mosaic() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#4575B4", "#ABD9E9", "#FEE090", "#F46D43")) +
  ggtitle("Health and Finances")
```

## geom_mosaic: setting the aesthetics

In
[`geom_mosaic()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/geom_mosaic.md),
the following aesthetics can be specified:

- `weight`: select a weighting variable

- `x`: select variables to add to formula

  - declared as `x = product(var2, var1, ...)`

- `alpha`: add an alpha transparency to the selected variable

  - unless the variable is called in `x`, it will be added to the
    formula in the first position

- `fill`: select a variable to be filled

  - unless the variable is called in `x`, it will be added to the
    formula in the first position after the optional `alpha` variable.

- `conds` : select a variable to condition on

  - declared as `conds = product(cond1, cond2, ...)`

These values are then sent through repurposed `productplots` functions
to create the desired formula: `weight ~ alpha + fill + x | conds`.

## Version compatibility issues with ggplot2

Since the initial release of ggmosaic, ggplot2 has evolved considerably.
And as ggplot2 continues to evolve, ggmosaic must continue to evolve
alongside it. Although these changes affect the underlying code and not
the general usage of ggmosaic, the general user may need to be aware of
compatibility issues that can arise between versions. The table below
summarizes the compatibility between versions.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`GeomMosaic`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/GeomMosaic.md)
  : Geom proto
- [`GeomMosaicJitter`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/GeomMosaicJitter.md)
  : Geom proto
- [`GeomMosaicText`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/GeomMosaicText.md)
  : Geom proto
- [`StatMosaic`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/StatMosaic.md)
  : Geom proto
- [`StatMosaicJitter`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/StatMosaicJitter.md)
  : Geom proto
- [`StatMosaicText`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/StatMosaicText.md)
  : Geom proto
- [`ddecker()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/ddecker.md)
  : Template for a double decker plot. A double decker plot is composed
  of a sequence of spines in the same direction, with the final spine in
  the opposite direction.
- [`fly`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/fly.md) :
  Flying Etiquette Survey Data
- [`geom_mosaic()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/geom_mosaic.md)
  [`stat_mosaic_text()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/geom_mosaic.md)
  [`stat_mosaic()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/geom_mosaic.md)
  : Mosaic plots.
- [`geom_mosaic_jitter()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/geom_mosaic_jitter.md)
  [`stat_mosaic_jitter()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/geom_mosaic_jitter.md)
  : Jittered dots in Mosaic plots.
- [`geom_mosaic_text()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/geom_mosaic_text.md)
  : Labeling for Mosaic plots.
- [`ggmosaic_app()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/ggmosaic_app.md)
  : Launch shiny app
- [`happy`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/happy.md)
  : Data related to happiness from the general social survey.
- [`hbar()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/hbar.md)
  : Horizontal bar partition: width constant, height varies.
- [`hspine()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/hspine.md)
  : Horizontal spine partition: height constant, width varies.
- [`mosaic()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/mosaic.md)
  : Template for a mosaic plot. A mosaic plot is composed of spines in
  alternating directions.
- [`product()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/product.md)
  : Wrapper for a list
- [`scale_type(`*`<productlist>`*`)`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/scale_type.productlist.md)
  : Helper function for determining scales
- [`scale_x_productlist()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/scale_x_productlist.md)
  [`scale_y_productlist()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/scale_x_productlist.md)
  [`ScaleContinuousProduct`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/scale_x_productlist.md)
  : Determining scales for mosaics
- [`spine()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/spine.md)
  : Spine partition: divide longest dimension.
- [`squeeze()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/squeeze.md)
  : Internal helper function
- [`theme_mosaic`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/theme_mosaic.md)
  : Theme for mosaic plots
- [`titanic`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/titanic.md)
  : Passengers and crew on board the Titanic
- [`vbar()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/vbar.md)
  : Vertical bar partition: height constant, width varies.
- [`vspine()`](https://haleyjeppson.github.io/ggmosaic/reference/vspine.md)
  : Vertical spine partition: width constant, height varies.
